items.text: Georgia has no adult-use cannabis. Its medical program lets registered patients and caregivers with a Medical Cannabis Patient Registry Card possess up to 12,000 mg of THC, bought only from Commission-licensed dispensaries or licensed independent pharmacies. Vape products are allowed but smoking cannabis is banned by state law. There is no reciprocity with other states: a card from another state may be recognised only if it allows the same possession as Georgia law and the holder has been in Georgia for less than 45 days, and visitors can't buy at Georgia dispensaries.

laws.rule: Under the Hands-Free Georgia Act (O.C.G.A. 40-6-241, from 1 July 2018), drivers may not hold or support a phone with any part of the body, write, read or send texts, emails or social media, watch video other than navigation, or record video (running dash cams excepted). Hands-free calls, voice-to-text, GPS and music set up before driving are allowed. The only stop exemption is for a lawfully parked vehicle.
laws.penalty_signal: US$50 and 1 point for a first conviction, US$100 and 2 points for a second and US$150 and 3 points for a third within 24 months (about A$71, A$142 and A$213 at A$1 = US$0.7040, RBA 30 Oct 2026); a first charge can be dropped by showing the court a hands-free device

laws.rule: Visitors with a foreign driver's licence don't need a Georgia licence unless they become Georgia residents. Carry the foreign licence, and a passport or visa, as police may ask for it to check the licence. The state drivers manual requires an International Driving Permit if the licence is not in English.

Cumberland Island National Seashore: no fires at the wilderness campsites; campfires only at Sea Camp and Stafford Beach in the fire rings. Hammocks must be free-standing (no tying to trees or structures). Carts and wheeled coolers are not allowed north of Sea Camp. Do not approach within 50 feet (about 15 m) of the wild horses. Only service animals are allowed in campgrounds. Propane tanks larger than 1 gallon are not allowed on the ferry.

The Georgia Insurance and Safety Fire Commissioner says that since 1 July 2015 consumer fireworks are legal in Georgia, with firecrackers, skyrockets and sparklers given as examples. It advises buying from a licensed fireworks dealer and following all state laws, and points to local police or fire departments for local rules on use.

layers.authority: US National Park Service, Cumberland Island National Seashore
layers.process: The island is reached only by the concession ferry from St Marys (or private boat); reservations are recommended and check-in starts 1 hour before departure at the mainland visitor centre. Entrance fee US$15 per person aged 16 and over (about A$21.30), valid 7 days, paid when checking in for the ferry; cashless. The ferry does not carry pets, kayaks or cars. Winter: no Tuesday or Wednesday ferry from 1 December to 28 February. Fees in US dollars; A$1 = USD 0.7040 (RBA, 30 Oct 2026), so US$1 is about A$1.42.

layers.authority: US National Park Service, Cumberland Island National Seashore
layers.process: A reservation is required to camp. Book on Recreation.gov up to six months ahead and print the permit within 10 days of the trip. Five campgrounds: Sea Camp, Stafford Beach and three wilderness sites (Hickory Hill, Yankee Paradise, Brickhill Bluff). Limits: 7 consecutive nights; 6 people per site. The wilderness area and its campsites are closed during managed hunts, October to January. Campers at Sea Camp must take the 10:15 am return ferry. Fees in US dollars; A$1 = USD 0.7040 (RBA, 30 Oct 2026), so US$1 is about A$1.42.
